subject.title: config: use datetime suffix for config backup files instead of numeric rotation

question: Should timestamped config backups preserve or convert existing numbered `.bak.N` recovery points, or may first-run cleanup delete them when the suffix scheme changes?
rationale: Config backups may be the user's only recovery copy, and repository policy treats config migration and recovery behavior as compatibility-sensitive rather than automation-only.

options.title: Preserve Or Convert Legacy Backups
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set without silently deleting recovery points.

options.title: Accept Timestamp-Only Cleanup
options.body: Allow first-run cleanup to prune legacy numbered backups, but document the upgrade behavior and accept the loss of old rollback slots.

options.title: Keep The Numbered Ring
options.body: Reject the timestamped naming change for now and keep the current numbered backup contract.

recommendation.title: Preserve Or Convert Legacy Backups
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to keep existing `.bak.N` files through migration or convert them into the timestamped retention set without silently deleting recovery points.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible history on the backup rotation helper and config recovery semantics.
